123	  intent: null,
124	  sessionId: null,
125	  discoveryTranscript: '',
126	  pinned: [],
127	  generationStatus: 'idle',
128	  generation: null,
129	  generationError: null,
130	  togglePin: (ref) =>
131	    set((state) => ({

135	    })),
136	  clearPins: () => set({ pinned: [] }),

140	  startGenerating: () => set({ generationStatus: 'generating', generationError: null }),

145	    set({ connectionState, connectionError }),
146	  setSessionId: (sessionId) => set({ sessionId }),
147	  setTranscriptState: (transcript, transcriptSegments) =>

150	      transcriptSegments,

154	    set((state) => ({

159	      intent,

content.text:
Done. Generate is wired end to end and verified in the browser.

## What landed

**Pin state lifted into the session store** — [session.ts](apps/web/src/stores/session.ts) now owns `pinned: PinnedRef[]` with `togglePin`/`clearPins`. [idea-board.tsx](apps/web/src/components/idea-board.tsx) pins through it with `imageUrl: null`; Lane B tiles will pass a real URL into the identical shape, no second path.

**The rail** — [pin-rail.tsx](apps/web/src/components/pin-rail.tsx), fixed above the docked mic, full width, borderless, labelled `N pins · conditioning input`. Absent at zero pins, animates in on `workspace-enter`/`sticker-enter`, no motion dependency. A borderless gradient scrim keeps it from colliding with the transcript's last lines.

**`POST /v1/generate`** — [synthesis.py](apps/api/glia/generation/synthesis.py) (one OpenAI call, `json_schema` out, `SynthesisedPrompt` Pydantic in — a malformed prompt is a refusal, never a truncation) then [fal.py](apps/api/glia/generation/fal.py) (queue submit + poll, `X-Fal-Store-IO: 0`, `Authorization: Key`, no submit retry, 45s cap → typed `timeout`, one generation in flight per session → typed `already_generating`). It follows fal's own `status_url`/`response_url` with the host pinned, which sidesteps the nested-model-id queue-path trap and keeps a trusted response from becoming an open fetch. No SDK, no webhook, no new dependency; `uv.lock` unchanged.

**Degradation, as specified** — every pin's title goes into the synthesis; only public-https pins go to fal as `image_urls`. The visible proof: with three stickers pinned the prompt ended `…echoing cobalt observatory, brutalist sun study, quiet mediterranean` and reported `0 reference images`; unpinning one dropped that phrase from the next prompt.

## Verified

Fixture mode, three pins → Generate → image took the workpane with the exact prompt underneath, model id and reference count. Unpin → label went to `2 pins`, regenerate, prompt changed. Zero pins → rail gone. `pnpm lint/typecheck/build`, `uv run ruff check .`, `uv run mypy .`, 58 pytest tests all pass. No key material or server-only endpoint in `dist/` (grepped the literal `.env` values, the variable names, and `queue.fal.run`).

## Two things you should know

**I could not exercise the live fal path.** `FAL_KEY` is empty in the local `.env`, so the network half is verified against a mocked httpx transport only — submit shape, headers, `image_urls`, the reference/fallback model split, the poll timeout, the single-flight refusal, and no-retry-on-submit each have a test. The first real key will be the first real submit. Fixture mode is genuinely offline: its image is an inline SVG data URI, and a test asserts the route opens no connection.

**Generate is only reachable with at least one pin,** since the rail is its only home and the rail is absent at zero. That follows the spec as written, but it means a pinless session can't generate — say the word if you want a fallback entry point.

Two unrelated frictions I hit and did not touch: discovery outranks the board, so once Cala answers the stickers vanish and there is nothing left to pin (I turned live discovery off to test); and the in-app browser blocks microphone access, so I drove the session with a synthetic audio stream rather than a real mic.

[idea-board.tsx](apps/web/src/components/idea-board.tsx) pins through it with `imageUrl: null`; Lane B tiles will pass a real URL into the identical shape, no second path.

**The rail** — [pin-rail.tsx](apps/web/src/components/pin-rail.tsx), fixed above the docked mic, full width, borderless, labelled `N pins · conditioning input`. Absent at zero pins, animates in on `workspace-enter`/`sticker-enter`, no motion dependency. A borderless gradient scrim keeps it from colliding with the transcript's last lines.

**`POST /v1/generate`** — [synthesis.py](apps/api/glia/generation/synthesis.py) (one OpenAI call, `json_schema` out, `SynthesisedPrompt` Pydantic in — a malformed prompt is a refusal, never a truncation) then [fal.py](apps/api/glia/generation/fal.py) (queue submit + poll, `X-Fal-Store-IO: 0`, `Authorization: Key`, no submit retry, 45s cap → typed `timeout`, one generation in flight per session → typed `already_generating`). It follows fal's own `status_url`/`response_url` with the host pinned, which sidesteps the nested-model-id queue-path trap and keeps a trusted response from becoming an open fetch. No SDK, no webhook, no new dependency; `uv.lock` unchanged.

**Degradation, as specified** — every pin's title goes into the synthesis; only public-https pins go to fal as `image_urls`. The visible proof: with three stickers pinned the prompt ended `…echoing cobalt observatory, brutalist sun study, quiet mediterranean` and reported `0 reference images`; unpinning one dropped that phrase from the next prompt.

## Verified

Fixture mode, three pins → Generate → image took the workpane with the exact prompt underneath, model id and reference count. Unpin → label went to `2 pins`, regenerate, prompt changed. Zero pins → rail gone. `pnpm lint/typecheck/build`, `uv run ruff check .`, `uv run mypy .`, 58 pytest tests all pass. No key material or server-only endpoint in `dist/` (grepped the literal `.env` values, the variable names, and `queue.fal.run`).

## Two things you should know

**I could not exercise the live fal path.** `FAL_KEY` is empty in the local `.env`, so the network half is verified against a mocked httpx transport only — submit shape, headers, `image_urls`, the reference/fallback model split, the poll timeout, the single-flight refusal, and no-retry-on-submit each have a test. The first real key will be the first real submit. Fixture mode is genuinely offline: its image is an inline SVG data URI, and a test asserts the route opens no connection.

**Generate is only reachable with at least one pin,** since the rail is its only home and the rail is absent at zero. That follows the spec as written, but it means a pinless session can't generate — say the word if you want a fallback entry point.

Two unrelated frictions I hit and did not touch: discovery outranks the board, so once Cala answers the stickers vanish and there is nothing left to pin (I turned live discovery off to test); and the in-app browser blocks microphone access, so I drove the session with a synthetic audio stream rather than a real mic.","background_tasks":[],"session_crons":[]}

    def test_websocket_reconciles_deltas_and_returns_stable_intent() -> None:
        with TestClient(app) as client, client.websocket_connect("/ws") as socket:
            ready = socket.receive_json()
            assert ready["type"] == "session.ready"
    
            socket.send_json(
                {
                    "type": "transcript.delta",
                    "event_id": "event-1",
                    "item_id": "item-1",
                    "delta": "A lonely cobalt ",
                }
            )
            accepted = socket.receive_json()
            assert accepted == {
                "type": "transcript.accepted",
                "item_id": "item-1",
                "transcript": "A lonely cobalt ",
                "complete": False,
            }
    
            socket.send_json(
                {
                    "type": "transcript.completed",
                    "event_id": "event-2",
                    "item_id": "item-1",
                    "transcript": "A lonely cobalt observatory, cinematic and cold",
                }
            )
            completed = socket.receive_json()
            intent = socket.receive_json()
    
        assert completed["type"] == "transcript.accepted"
        assert completed["complete"] is True
        assert intent["type"] == "intent.updated"
        assert intent["stable"] is True

import pathlib
p = pathlib.Path("tests/test_generate.py")
s = p.read_text()

s = s.replace("""from glia.generation.fal import FalClient, FalTimedOut, is_public_https, reference_urls""",
"""from glia.generation.fal import (
    FalClient,
    FalReferenceUnavailable,
    FalTimedOut,
    is_public_https,
    reference_urls,
)""")

s += '''

# ─── a reference fal cannot fetch ───────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Measured against the live API on 29 Aug 2026. fal marks such a request COMPLETED on the
# status endpoint and only rejects it from the *result* endpoint, with a 422 carrying
# `detail[].type == "file_download_error"`. Both halves of that are load-bearing, so both are
# pinned here — a status poll that believed COMPLETED and a result fetch that read the 422 as a
# generic upstream error is exactly the bug this replaced.

_DOWNLOAD_FAILURE: dict[str, Any] = {
    "detail": [
        {
            "loc": ["body", "image_urls"],
            "msg": "Failed to download the file.",
            "type": "file_download_error",
            "input": ["https://upload.wikimedia.org/example.jpg"],
        }
    ]
}


def _unfetchable_reference(request: httpx.Request) -> httpx.Response:
    if request.method == "POST":
        return httpx.Response(
            200,
            json={
                "request_id": "req-1",
                "status_url": "https://queue.fal.run/fal-ai/flux-pro/requests/req-1/status",
                "response_url": "https://queue.fal.run/fal-ai/flux-pro/requests/req-1",
            },
        )
    if request.url.path.endswith("/status"):
        # fal really does say COMPLETED here for a request it rejected.
        return httpx.Response(200, json={"status": "COMPLETED"})
    return httpx.Response(422, json=_DOWNLOAD_FAILURE)


def test_an_unfetchable_reference_is_its_own_answer(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    stub_transport(_unfetchable_reference, monkeypatch)
    fal = FalClient(settings())
    synthesiser = _StubSynthesiser()
    with client_for(fal, synthesiser=synthesiser) as http:
        response = http.post("/v1/generate", json=body())

    payload = response.json()
    # A 200 with a typed status, not a 502: retrying cannot help, and the prompt is still worth
    # showing. The reference count reports what we tried to send, not what fal accepted.
    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert payload["status"] == "reference_unavailable"
    assert payload["image_url"] is None
    assert payload["prompt"] == synthesiser.prompt
    assert payload["reference_count"] == 1


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_unfetchable_reference_is_not_a_generic_upstream_error(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    stub_transport(_unfetchable_reference, monkeypatch)
    fal = FalClient(settings())
    with pytest.raises(FalReferenceUnavailable):
        await fal.generate(
            model="fal-ai/flux-pro/kontext/max/multi",
            prompt="a cold sea",
            references=["https://upload.wikimedia.org/example.jpg"],
        )


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_an_ordinary_422_is_still_an_upstream_error(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    def handler(request: httpx.Request) -> httpx.Response:
        if request.method == "POST":
            return httpx.Response(422, json={"detail": [{"type": "value_error", "loc": []}]})
        raise AssertionError("a rejected submit is never polled")

    stub_transport(handler, monkeypatch)
    fal = FalClient(settings())
    with pytest.raises(FalUpstreamError):
        await fal.generate(model="fal-ai/flux/schnell", prompt="a cold sea", references=[])

content.text:
Done. The rail is now a bottom banner and, since `FAL_KEY` appeared mid-session, I used it to close the live gap — which turned up two real problems.

## The layout change

The rail is fixed to the floor of the viewport, full width, on its own white ground with a hairline top edge so it reads as one contained thing. The mic composer now docks *above* it, and nothing is overlapped: one `--rail-space` variable reserves the strip in the workspace grid, the transcript's padding and the mic's dock offset, and `:has(.pin-rail)` applies it only while there is a rail. Each tile carries a black X badge on its corner — always visible, not on hover — and the tiles scroll sideways rather than wrapping so the banner's height stays a constant the layout can reserve. Verified at desktop and mobile: pin, unpin from the banner, regenerate, zero pins hides it.

## Two things live fal exposed

**fal cannot fetch `upload.wikimedia.org`.** It answers a blank User-Agent — which is what fal's fetcher sends — with `403`, so fal returns `file_download_error`. This matters beyond today: `docs/PARTNERS.md` names Wikimedia Commons as a primary Lane B source, and those URLs will not work as reference images. Lane B will need a re-host (fal's own `upload_file`) or a different source.

**My client mishandled that, and the fix is a real improvement.** fal marks such a request `COMPLETED` on the status endpoint and only rejects it with a `422` from the *result* endpoint. My code logged both endpoints identically and collapsed the failure into "temporarily unavailable" — misleading, because retrying can never help. There is now a typed `reference_unavailable` status carrying the prompt and reference count, and the rail says *"One pinned image could not be fetched for conditioning — unpin it to generate without it."* That is the one generation failure the user can actually act on. Three tests pin the behaviour, including that an ordinary 422 stays a generic upstream error.

## Live-verified against real fal

Text-only via `flux/schnell` (13.8s). Reference-conditioned via `flux-pro/kontext/max/multi` with `image_urls` (21.8s) — the conditioning path works, which was the single most important unproven claim. The typed reference failure. And two concurrent clicks on one session: first `ok`, second `already_generating`. That cost about six generations on your prepaid balance.

`pnpm lint/typecheck/build`, `ruff`, `mypy --strict`, 61 pytest tests all pass. No key material in `dist/` (grepped all four literal values plus the names).

## Two things you should know

**I killed your dev server.** My cleanup used `pkill -f "uvicorn glia.main:app"`, which matched your `--reload` server on port 8000 running from the main checkout, not just mine — probably two or three times over the session. It is running now and I left it untouched; I moved to port 8010 once I noticed. Sorry about that.

**`.env` changed under me at 16:13** — `DEMO_MODE` went `fixture` → `live` and `FAL_KEY` was filled in. That flipped `test_websocket_reconciles_deltas_and_returns_stable_intent` red, because it asserted `source == "fixture"` while reading ambient config. I gave it a fixture that pins `DEMO_MODE` for the duration, so flipping the env no longer turns the suite red.

One thing I could not do: a live screenshot of the full loop in the browser, because port 8000 is yours and the frontend's API base URL is baked in at build time. The browser loop is fully verified in fixture mode, and the live route is verified by direct calls.

# ship-it — consolidate finished work into develop, then clean up safely

Purpose: when a piece of work is DONE, get it safely stored in `develop` through
a merged PR (so CI history stays clean going forward), then remove the leftover
branch and worktree so junk doesn't pile up and eat disk.

Two phases with different rules:
- **Consolidate** (push → PR → squash-merge → pull develop): additive only,
  never destroys anything. Run directly, no confirmation.
- **Clean up** (delete branch, remove worktree): the only irreversible part.
  Governed by a hard safety gate — NEVER delete anything whose content is not
  already provably inside `develop`. The gate protects against losing code; it
  is an automatic check, not a "do you want to?" prompt.

The overriding rule: **do not delete code that isn't consolidated.** If any work
is not yet in `develop`, STOP, report exactly what's unconsolidated, and delete
nothing.

## Prerequisites (verify first)

Run these checks before doing anything destructive. Report and stop if any fail.

1. `gh` CLI is installed and authenticated: `gh auth status`. If missing, tell
   the user to install it (`brew install gh && gh auth login`) — do NOT fall
   back to raw API token entry.
2. You are inside the correct repo. From the current dir:
   `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`. Confirm it's `master-platform` or
   `master-infra` (never mix the two — this repo has separate git roots).
3. Identify the current branch: `git branch --show-current`. It must NOT be
   `develop`, `master`, or `main`. Abort if it is.
4. Confirm the base branch. Default base is `develop` for this monorepo. Only
   use a different base if the user says so.

## Workflow (run in this order)

### 0. Scope + "nothing left behind" guard (do NOT ask for confirmation)
Invoking this skill IS the user's consent to ship. Run directly — do not ask
"ready to proceed?". Print a one-line scope summary (repo, branch, base, commits
ahead) and continue. But first make sure nothing gets left unconsolidated:
```
git fetch origin <base>
git status --porcelain                       # uncommitted / untracked work?
git rev-list --count origin/<base>..HEAD     # commits to ship
```
Handle each case:
- **Current branch is `develop`/`master`/`main`** → ABORT. This skill ships a
  feature branch INTO develop; it must not run from the base branch.
- **Uncommitted or untracked changes exist** → this is unconsolidated work. Do
  NOT proceed to any deletion. Commit it (sensible message) so it becomes part
  of what gets shipped, then continue. Never `git stash`-and-forget or discard.
- **0 commits ahead of base** → nothing to ship. Tell the user and STOP (don't
  create an empty PR, don't delete anything).
Only once the branch is clean (no uncommitted work) and has ≥1 commit ahead do
you continue to step 1.

### 1. Push and create the PR
```
git push -u origin HEAD
gh pr create --base <base> --head <current-branch> \
  --title "<title>" --body "<body>" --fill
```
- Use `--fill` to derive title/body from commits unless the user gave a title.
- If a PR already exists for the branch, reuse it: `gh pr view --json number,url`.

### 2. Squash-and-merge with admin override (bypass CI)
```
gh pr merge <current-branch> --squash --admin

# --delete-branch is deliberately NOT used. Run from a worktree, gh's post-merge
# checkout step fails with "fatal: 'develop' is already used by worktree", and
# --delete-branch never runs: the merge lands server-side but the remote branch
# survives silently. Delete it as its own step, and PROVE it is gone.
gh pr view <current-branch> --json state -q .state    # must print MERGED
git push origin --delete <current-branch>
git fetch --prune origin
if git ls-remote --exit-code --heads origin <current-branch> >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "REMOTE_BRANCH_SURVIVED: stop, do not clean up the worktree"
else
  echo "REMOTE_BRANCH_DELETED"
fi
```
- `--admin` bypasses required status checks / failing CI. This is intentional
  and matches the user's request — do not wait for CI, do not block on it.
- `--delete-branch` deletes the REMOTE branch as part of the merge.
- If `--admin` is rejected (insufficient permissions), report exactly that and
  stop — do NOT silently retry without admin or force-push over branch
  protection. Ask the user how to proceed.

### 3. Pull develop
```
git checkout <base>
git pull origin <base>
```
This brings the squashed commit into your local base branch.

## CLEANUP SAFETY GATE (read before steps 4–5)
From here on you delete things. Apply this gate to EVERY delete. Deletion is
allowed ONLY when the target's own work is provably already in `origin/<base>`.

Why the naive checks are wrong:
- `git branch --merged` uses SHA reachability → after a squash-merge the branch's
  commits aren't reachable from develop, so it falsely reports "not merged".
- `git diff <branch> origin/<base>` compares full trees → if develop advanced for
  ANY other reason (another branch merged, someone else's commit), the trees
  differ even though THIS branch's work is fully consolidated. False positive.
- `git diff` WITHOUT `--binary` cannot represent a binary file: it emits the
  placeholder `Binary files a/path and b/path differ`, which `git apply` refuses
  with `cannot apply binary patch to '<path>' without full index line`. Any repo
  that commits a built artifact then fails the gate on EVERY run, even when the
  branch is fully merged. Always pass `--binary`.

Correct, portable check (works on git ≥2.20, no merge-tree needed) — ask only
"are THIS branch's net changes already present in develop?", ignoring whatever
else moved develop. Take the branch's diff since its merge-base and test whether
it REVERSE-applies cleanly to the current develop working tree; if it does,
develop already contains those changes.

A green from this gate authorises `git worktree remove` and `git branch -D`.
That makes it the one gate in this skill whose FALSE POSITIVE destroys work.
Treat it accordingly: the command must name the place it runs, and it must be
proven able to go red in the same run.

The failure this replaces: `git apply --reverse --check` resolves paths against
the CURRENT directory. Run from the worktree — still on the branch — it
reverse-applies the branch's own patch to the branch's own tree, which always
succeeds. Vacuous green. Telling the agent in prose to "run it from develop" is
not enough; put the location inside the command.

Precondition: step 3 already left the MAIN checkout on an up-to-date `<base>`
with a clean working tree. The gate validates that itself and refuses to answer
otherwise — a gate that runs in the wrong place is worse than no gate:
```
MAIN=$(git worktree list --porcelain | head -1 | cut -d' ' -f2)   # first entry is always the main checkout
BASE=$(git merge-base origin/<base> <current-branch>)

if [ "$(git -C "$MAIN" rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)" != "<base>" ]; then
  echo "GATE_INVALID: main checkout is not on <base>"
elif [ -n "$(git -C "$MAIN" status --porcelain)" ]; then
  echo "GATE_INVALID: main checkout is dirty"
elif [ "$(git -C "$MAIN" rev-parse HEAD)" != "$(git -C "$MAIN" rev-parse origin/<base>)" ]; then
  echo "GATE_INVALID: main checkout is behind origin/<base>"
else
  git diff --binary "$BASE" <current-branch> > /tmp/ship-it-consolidation.patch
  if [ ! -s /tmp/ship-it-consolidation.patch ]; then
    echo CONSOLIDATED          # branch made no net change
  elif git -C "$MAIN" apply --reverse --check /tmp/ship-it-consolidation.patch 2>/dev/null; then
    echo CONSOLIDATED          # develop already contains every net change
  else
    echo NOT_CONSOLIDATED
  fi
fi
```
There are THREE outcomes, not two: consolidated, not consolidated, and NOT
MEASURED. `GATE_INVALID` is the third. It is a STOP, never an override, and
collapsing it into either of the other two is exactly how a vacuous green ships.

### Prove the gate can go red — same run, every run (mandatory)

Before trusting a CONSOLIDATED, confirm the gate is capable of saying the other
thing. The control MUST be git-generated. A hand-written patch is rejected with
`corrupt patch at line N` — a rejection of FORM, not of content. It proves the
patch parser works and says nothing about whether the gate detects absent
changes. A control that cannot fail for the reason you care about is not a
control. A control run once when this skill was written says nothing about the
run happening now, in a different directory.
```
f=$(git diff --name-only "$BASE" <current-branch> | head -1)
git -C "$MAIN" show "origin/<base>:$f" > /tmp/ctl.orig 2>/dev/null || : > /tmp/ctl.orig
{ echo "ship-it negative control marker"; cat /tmp/ctl.orig; } > /tmp/ctl.new
git diff --no-index --binary /tmp/ctl.orig /tmp/ctl.new \
  | sed "s#/tmp/ctl.orig#a/$f#; s#/tmp/ctl.new#b/$f#" > /tmp/ship-it-control.patch
if git -C "$MAIN" apply --reverse --check /tmp/ship-it-control.patch 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "CONTROL_FAILED: the gate greens a change that is absent from <base>"
else
  echo "CONTROL_OK: the gate can go red"
fi
```
Anything other than `CONTROL_OK` means the gate carries no information in this
run. STOP. Remove nothing, delete no branch, and say in the report that the
consolidation verdict was unproven.
`--binary` is load-bearing, not cosmetic: without it the gate is structurally
unable to describe a binary file and reports NOT_CONSOLIDATED for reasons that
have nothing to do with whether the work shipped.

Corroborating per-path blob check (run it whenever the patch gate says
NOT_CONSOLIDATED, and any time the branch touches binaries). It compares content
hashes directly, so it handles binaries head-on and does not depend on patch
application at all — a path that prints nothing is byte-identical in develop:
```
git diff --name-only -z "$BASE" <current-branch> | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
  a=$(git rev-parse --quiet --verify "<current-branch>:$f" 2>/dev/null || echo MISSING)
  b=$(git rev-parse --quiet --verify "origin/<base>:$f" 2>/dev/null || echo MISSING)
  [ "$a" = "$b" ] || echo "DIFFERS $f"
done
```
(Use the `-z` / `read -d ''` form rather than `for f in $(git diff --name-only)`:
unquoted word-splitting shatters a path containing a space into phantom entries
that all report DIFFERS. `MISSING` on both sides means the branch deleted the
path and develop did too — consolidated.)

Interpretation:
- **CONSOLIDATED** (empty patch, or reverse-applies cleanly) → every net change
  the branch made is already in develop → safe to delete branch and worktree.
- **NOT_CONSOLIDATED** → DIAGNOSE IT BEFORE YOU TRUST IT OR OVERRIDE IT. Read
  `git apply`'s stderr (re-run without `2>/dev/null`): a genuine miss reports
  `patch does not apply` against text hunks, whereas the binary-representation
  bug above names a binary path and a missing index line. The two look identical
  if you only read the verdict. Corroborate with the blob check, then:
  - Blob check prints nothing → the branch's content IS in develop; the verdict
    was an artifact of the check, not unconsolidated work.
  - Blob check prints `DIFFERS` → treat as real. STOP. Show what's missing with
    `git log --oneline origin/<base>..<current-branch>` and
    `git diff origin/<base>...<current-branch>`, report clearly, and delete
    NOTHING — neither branch nor worktree. Not losing this work is the point.

If the two checks disagree, or you cannot explain the failure, **delete nothing**.
The default when a gate fails is always to preserve; diagnosing is how you earn a
CONSOLIDATED verdict, never a reason to skip the gate or force a deletion.

One residual case both checks share: if develop MODIFIED a file after the merge
that this branch also touched, both report NOT_CONSOLIDATED / DIFFERS even though
the branch shipped. For text the reverse-apply usually still succeeds on context,
but a binary is matched whole-blob, so a rebuilt artifact on develop will trip it.
That is the safe direction — the checks can withhold a deletion they could have
allowed, but they will not call unconsolidated work consolidated. Confirm such a
case by hand (e.g. the squash commit in `git log origin/<base> -- <path>`) before
concluding anything.

This is immune to a develop that moved underneath you, because it inspects only
the branch's own diff, never the full tree.

### 4. Delete the local branch (only if the gate passed)
```
git branch -D <current-branch>
```
`-D` is used because after a squash-merge git's own `-d` merged-check would
refuse — but we've already proven consolidation by content above, so this is
safe. If the content gate did NOT pass, do not run this.

### 5. Worktree cleanup (only if the gate passed)
Worktrees in this repo live under `.claude/worktrees/`. Clean up the worktree
that hosted the merged branch so it stops taking disk. But re-apply the gate per
worktree — a worktree may hold work that never made it into develop.
```
git worktree list
```
For the worktree tied to the merged branch, verify BOTH:
- Working tree clean: `git -C <worktree-path> status --porcelain` is empty
  (no uncommitted/untracked files).
- Commits consolidated: apply the same reverse-apply check to the worktree's
  HEAD, so a moved develop doesn't cause a false block:
  ```
  WT_BASE=$(git -C <worktree-path> merge-base origin/<base> HEAD)
  git -C <worktree-path> diff --binary "$WT_BASE" HEAD > /tmp/ship-it-wt.patch
  # test against up-to-date develop (main checkout is on <base> from step 3)
  if [ ! -s /tmp/ship-it-wt.patch ] || \
     git -C "$MAIN" apply --reverse --check /tmp/ship-it-wt.patch 2>/dev/null; then
    echo WT_CONSOLIDATED
  else
    echo WT_NOT_CONSOLIDATED
  fi
  ```
  `git -C "$MAIN"` is load-bearing here, exactly like `--binary`. Run the apply
  from the worktree and you are testing the branch against itself: it always
  says WT_CONSOLIDATED, and on the other side of that green is
  `git worktree remove`. `$MAIN` comes from the branch gate above, where it was
  validated; if that gate did not run in this same shell, re-derive and
  re-validate it before using it here.
  `--binary` here for the same reason as the branch gate — without it a committed
  binary artifact makes every worktree read WT_NOT_CONSOLIDATED. On
  WT_NOT_CONSOLIDATED, diagnose before trusting it: read `git apply`'s stderr and
  corroborate with the same per-path blob check, substituting the worktree's HEAD:
  ```
  git -C <worktree-path> diff --name-only -z "$WT_BASE" HEAD | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
    a=$(git -C <worktree-path> rev-parse --quiet --verify "HEAD:$f" 2>/dev/null || echo MISSING)
    b=$(git rev-parse --quiet --verify "origin/<base>:$f" 2>/dev/null || echo MISSING)
    [ "$a" = "$b" ] || echo "DIFFERS $f"
  done
  ```

Then:
- **Both pass** (clean tree AND WT_CONSOLIDATED) → the worktree holds nothing that
  isn't in develop. Remove it:
  ```
  git worktree remove <worktree-path>
  ```
- **Either fails** → treat it as unconsolidated work (dirty/untracked files, or
  commits not in develop). STOP. List exactly what's uncommitted/undelivered and
  remove NOTHING. Never `--force` a worktree removal that would discard work.

  the check misreading, not surviving work — say so explicitly in the report and
  only then treat the worktree as removable. A dirty working tree is never
  overridable this way: uncommitted files are unconsolidated by definition.

(safe — only removes metadata, never live files):
```
git worktree prune -v
```

End with a tight summary: PR URL, merge SHA on develop, branch deleted (remote +
local), and worktree status (removed / KEPT-with-reason). If the cleanup gate
blocked any deletion, lead with that: state clearly what work was NOT
consolidated and was therefore preserved, so nothing looks silently skipped.

content.content:
--- ae38db99bb6c7fc60c4c470b4f4074162d8ab4bf
feat(discovery): wire the transcript to Cala and render cited sources in the workpane (#4)

* feat(discovery): proxy cala entity resolution and cited source search

One Cala call site behind three budget gates. A settled turn resolves the spoken
subject with GET /entities, then asks POST /knowledge/search for a cited answer,
and the explainability references are joined onto context ids so the UI can show
which evidence actually carried it.

Credits are the only scarce resource here, so the controls are the feature:
a per-session debounce that replays instead of re-querying, a TTL cache keyed on
the normalised input that retains the raw JSON, and a ledger with a hard stop that
refuses rather than overdrawing. Entity calls are counted apart from search calls
because PARTNERS.md records it as undocumented whether they bill; they are charged
against the budget anyway, which is the safe direction.

429 and 422 are answers rather than failures and are never retried. Upstream bodies
are logged, never returned — errors leave as RFC 9457 problem documents.

Entire-Checkpoint: 01M16S0Z0C6VP5D0WBT0WGCE67

* feat(web): render cala's resolved entity, answer and evidence in the workpane

A settled turn asks the backend what the speaker means and the workpane shows
the reply: the resolved entity and its type, the answer as markdown, then one
card per piece of quoted evidence carrying its publisher and a link to the
document it came from. Items that explainability referenced are marked and
sorted first, because which evidence carried the answer is the interesting part.

The trigger is a new `settledTranscript` in the store, written only when the
backend marks a turn stable. Interim deltas move `transcript` many times a
second and now leave the query key alone, so they cannot spend a credit; a
repeated turn cannot either. The server debounces independently — the browser
is not the thing holding the budget.

Markdown renders through react-markdown with raw HTML left off, which is the
sanitisation. Publishers are text, never remote favicons: fetching a third
party image to decorate a citation is a tracking pixel.

cd /Users/nectios/workspace-os/hackathons/glia/glia/.claude/worktrees/waveform-layout-transition-6a7cdc
git add apps/api/glia/api.py apps/api/glia/config.py apps/api/glia/contracts.py apps/api/glia/generation apps/api/tests/test_api.py apps/api/tests/test_generate.py packages/api-client
git commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
feat(generate): synthesise one prompt and generate one image from the pinned session

POST /v1/generate turns a session into an image in two steps. OpenAI writes one
image prompt from the transcript, the distilled VisualIntent and the pin titles;
fal generates from it. The raw transcript never reaches fal — summarising it is
the point of the step, because speech is personal.

The prompt is a deliverable, not an internal, so it is constrained rather than
trusted: JSON schema on the way out, a Pydantic model with a hard 80-word cap on
the way back. A prompt that misses those bounds is a refusal, never a silent
truncation — if we cannot show it verbatim we do not send it.

Pins are a real input, and honestly so. Every pin's title goes into the synthesis;
only pins carrying a public https URL additionally go to fal as image_urls against
flux-pro/kontext/max/multi, and a session without any falls back to flux/schnell.
reference_count reports what fal actually received, so a board sticker — inline SVG
with no public URL — is never passed off as conditioning it was not.

fal is plain httpx against the REST queue: Authorization: Key, X-Fal-Store-IO: 0 on
every call, and the submit is never retried because a duplicate submit is a second
billed generation for one click. status_url and response_url are followed from fal's
own reply rather than constructed — the queue paths truncate a nested model id to its
app — with the host pinned so a trusted response cannot become an open fetch. No
webhook: it needs a publicly reachable callback and we are on localhost.

Three outcomes are answers rather than server errors, and each carries the prompt.
A ~45s poll cap returns a typed timeout. fal allows two concurrent requests on a new
account, so exactly one generation is in flight per session and the second click is
refused rather than queued. And reference_unavailable, measured live on 29 Aug 2026:
fal reports an unfetchable reference as COMPLETED on the status endpoint and rejects
it only from the result endpoint with a 422 carrying file_download_error. That is the
one generation failure the user can act on — the pin is theirs to remove — so it says
so instead of claiming a transient fault that retrying could fix.
upload.wikimedia.org is a live instance of it: it answers fal's blank User-Agent
with a 403, which Lane B will have to work around.

demo_mode="fixture" holds with the network unplugged: the prompt is composed from
the same three inputs by hand and the image is an inline SVG data URI, visibly a
stand-in rather than something passed off as generated. The model id says fixture:
so the one field whose job is to name what produced the image does not lie.

No new dependency; httpx and openai were already here. The websocket intent test
now pins DEMO_MODE for itself, so flipping the ambient .env to live no longer turns
a green suite red.
MSG
git log --oneline -1

lastPrompt: /anthropic-skills:ship-it into main branch

cd /Users/nectios/workspace-os/hackathons/glia/glia/.claude/worktrees/waveform-layout-transition-6a7cdc
git add apps/web/src
git commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
feat(web): lift pins into the session and add the generate rail and result view

Pinning was local state on the idea board. A pin is a conditioning input for
Generate, so it belongs to the session: the store owns `pinned: PinnedRef[]` with
togglePin and clearPins, and the board, the rail and the request all read it from
one place. Stickers pin with imageUrl: null because inline SVG has no public URL
that fal could fetch; Lane B's tiles will carry a real https URL through the
identical field, which is why there is one pin path rather than two.

The rail is a banner on the floor of the viewport, full width, below the docked
microphone, on its own light ground so the thumbnails and the button that consumes
them read as one control. Nothing above it is overlapped: a single --rail-space
variable reserves the strip in the workspace grid, the transcript's padding and the
microphone's dock offset, applied only while there is a rail to apply it for. Each
thumbnail carries a visible unpin badge rather than one revealed on hover — half of
what this rail is for is taking a pin back out. It is absent entirely at zero pins.

The label reads "N pins · conditioning input" rather than "Pinned" because that is
the causal claim being made, and the backend keeps it: the titles reach the prompt
whether or not the images reach fal.

The generated image takes the workpane with the prompt printed verbatim beneath it
in small muted type, next to the model id and the reference count. Not a caption and
never truncated — it is the exact string that produced the image above it, and a
shortened one would be a different claim. Zero references is stated plainly rather
than hidden. The result holds the pane until the next generation lands, so a failure

gh pr create --base main --head claude/pin-rail-generate-ea20be \
 --title "feat(generate): pin rail and Generate — pins become a real conditioning input" \
 --body "$(cat <<'MD'
Generate is the last beat of the demo: the transcript, the distilled idea and the images you kept become one prompt and one original image.

## Two properties this is built around

**Pins are a real input.** The rail says `conditioning input`, and the backend keeps that claim. Every pin's title goes into the prompt synthesis; every pin carrying a public https URL additionally goes to fal as `image_urls` against `flux-pro/kontext/max/multi`. A session with none falls back to `flux/schnell`, and `reference_count` reports what fal actually received — a board sticker is inline SVG with no public URL, so it steers the words and is never passed off as conditioning the pixels.

**The prompt is a deliverable.** Whatever goes to fal is shown to the user verbatim beneath the image. It is constrained rather than trusted — JSON schema out, a Pydantic model with a hard 80-word cap back — so a malformed prompt is a validation error, not a silent truncation. If we cannot show it, we do not send it.

## Backend

`POST /v1/generate` → one OpenAI synthesis (`OPENAI_SYNTHESIS_MODEL`), then fal over plain httpx against the REST queue. No SDK, no new dependency, `uv.lock` unchanged.

- `Authorization: Key`, `X-Fal-Store-IO: 0` on every call.
- Submit is never retried — a duplicate submit is a second billed generation for one click.
- `status_url` / `response_url` are followed from fal's own reply rather than constructed (the queue paths truncate a nested model id to its app), with the host pinned so a trusted response cannot become an open fetch.
- No webhook: it needs a publicly reachable callback and we are on localhost. The queue is polled on a ~45s cap.
- Exactly one generation in flight per session; fal allows two concurrent requests on a new account, so a second click is refused rather than queued.

Three typed outcomes are answers rather than server errors, and each carries the prompt: `timeout`, `already_generating`, and `reference_unavailable`.

## Found while verifying against live fal

fal reports a reference it cannot fetch as `COMPLETED` on the status endpoint, and rejects it only from the **result** endpoint with a 422 carrying `file_download_error`. Collapsing that into a generic "temporarily unavailable" was both wrong and unhelpful, since retrying can never fix it — hence the typed `reference_unavailable`, which tells the user to unpin the offending image.

The live instance of it: **`upload.wikimedia.org` answers a blank User-Agent with 403**, which is what fal's fetcher sends. `docs/PARTNERS.md` names Wikimedia Commons as a primary Lane B source, so Lane B will need a re-host or a different source for its reference URLs.

## Frontend

Pin state moves out of `idea-board.tsx` into the session store as `pinned: PinnedRef[]`. The rail is a bottom banner below the mic composer, absent at zero pins, with a visible unpin badge per thumbnail and a single Generate button. The generated image takes the workpane with the prompt verbatim underneath, next to the model id and reference count. Entry animation only, through the existing CSS conventions — the motion dependency is not resurrected.

## Verification

Live against real fal: text-only (`flux/schnell`, 13.8s), reference-conditioned (`kontext/max/multi` with `image_urls`, 21.8s), the typed reference failure, and two concurrent clicks on one session (first `ok`, second `already_generating`).

Fixture mode holds with the network unplugged — the prompt is composed by hand from the same three inputs and the image is an inline SVG data URI, with the model id reported as `fixture:<model>` so that field does not lie.

`pnpm lint / typecheck / build`, `ruff check .`, `mypy --strict`, 61 pytest tests pass. No key material in `dist/` — grepped the literal values of all four provider keys plus their names.

## Test plan

- [x] Pin three stickers → Generate → image in the workpane with the exact prompt beneath it
- [x] Unpin one → regenerate → the prompt visibly changes
- [x] Zero pins hides the rail
- [x] Second click while one is running is refused, not queued
- [x] Fixture mode returns a canned result with no network
- [x] Live fal, both models and both failure modes
- [ ] Live run driven by a real microphone (the in-app browser blocks device capture; the session was driven with a synthetic audio stream)
MD
)" 2>&1 | tail -3

A session with none falls back to `flux/schnell`, and `reference_count` reports what fal actually received — a board sticker is inline SVG with no public URL, so it steers the words and is never passed off as conditioning the pixels.

**The prompt is a deliverable.** Whatever goes to fal is shown to the user verbatim beneath the image. - Submit is never retried — a duplicate submit is a second billed generation for one click.
- `status_url` / `response_url` are followed from fal's own reply rather than constructed (the queue paths truncate a nested model id to its app), with the host pinned so a trusted response cannot become an open fetch.
- No webhook: it needs a publicly reachable callback and we are on localhost. The queue is polled on a ~45s cap.
- Exactly one generation in flight per session; fal allows two concurrent requests on a new account, so a second click is refused rather than queued.

fal reports a reference it cannot fetch as `COMPLETED` on the status endpoint, and rejects it only from the **result** endpoint with a 422 carrying `file_download_error`. Collapsing that into a generic "temporarily unavailable" was both wrong and unhelpful, since retrying can never fix it — hence the typed `reference_unavailable`, which tells the user to unpin the offending image.

cd /Users/nectios/workspace-os/hackathons/glia/glia/.claude/worktrees/waveform-layout-transition-6a7cdc
git add apps/api/glia/api.py apps/api/glia/config.py apps/api/tests/test_api.py packages/api-client
git commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
Merge origin/main into the generate branch

Lane B landed on main while this was in flight, so the two meet here. All three
conflicts were additive and both sides are kept: Lane B's discovery and image-proxy
settings sit beside the fal block in config.py, and its `/api/image` route beside
`/v1/generate` in api.py.

test_api.py takes main's version wholesale. Main had independently pinned DEMO_MODE
for the websocket intent test with an inline try/finally, which does the same job as
the fixture added here; the incumbent stays and the duplicate goes, leaving that file
byte-identical to main.

The api-client schema is regenerated against the merged backend, so it now carries
Lane B's contracts alongside the generate ones.

Lane B arriving is what PinnedRef was shaped for: its tiles carry a real https URL
through the same field the board's stickers leave null, so they reach fal as actual
reference images with no second pin path. Worth knowing before that is wired up —
measured live on 29 Aug 2026 — fal cannot fetch upload.wikimedia.org, which answers
its blank User-Agent with a 403. Commons URLs will need re-hosting to condition a
generation; until then they degrade to prompt steering and report reference_count 0.
MSG
git log --oneline -4
echo "=== conflicts remaining ==="; git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U || echo "(none)"
